LESSON: ORAL HYGIENE 1.0 HEALTH

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Oral hygiene 1.0 Health

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Oral hygiene 1.0 Health. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Oral hygiene 1.0 Health means using everyday Kenyan examples
2. describe how Oral hygiene 1.0 Health appears at home, school, or in the environment
3. practise one safe skill connected to Oral hygiene 1.0 Health
4. tell why Oral hygiene 1.0 Health matters for life in Kenya

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ORAL HYGIENE 1.0 HEALTH
Subject: HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Oral hygiene 1.0 Health helps you succeed in HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: ORAL HYGIENE 1.0 HEALTH
Oral hygiene 1.0 Health is part of Science learning. Connect every idea to something you can observe.
Use safe examples only. Do not try dangerous experiments without a teacher.
Write definitions in your own words, then add one drawing or real-life example.

PART 1: Explain what Oral hygiene 1.0 Health means using everyday Kenyan examples

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Oral hygiene 1.0 Health means using everyday Kenyan examples. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Oral hygiene 1.0 Health means using everyday Kenyan examples.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Oral hygiene 1.0 Health” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Oral hygiene 1.0 Health means using everyday Kenyan examples. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe how Oral hygiene 1.0 Health appears at home, school, or in the environment

What this means
In this part you learn to describe how Oral hygiene 1.0 Health appears at home, school, or in the environment. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe how Oral hygiene 1.0 Health appears at home, school, or in the environment.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Oral hygiene 1.0 Health matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe how Oral hygiene 1.0 Health appears at home, school, or in the environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise one safe skill connected to Oral hygiene 1.0 Health

What this means
In this part you learn to practise one safe skill connected to Oral hygiene 1.0 Health. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise one safe skill connected to Oral hygiene 1.0 Health.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Oral hygiene 1.0 Health this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise one safe skill connected to Oral hygiene 1.0 Health. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Tell why Oral hygiene 1.0 Health matters for life in Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to tell why Oral hygiene 1.0 Health matters for life in Kenya. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: tell why Oral hygiene 1.0 Health matters for life in Kenya.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Oral hygiene 1.0 Health” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can tell why Oral hygiene 1.0 Health matters for life in Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Oral hygiene 1.0 Health is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Oral hygiene 1.0 Health” around your school. (skill: explain what Oral hygiene 1.0 Health means using everyday Kenyan examples)

Example 2: Say why Oral hygiene 1.0 Health matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: describe how Oral hygiene 1.0 Health appears at home, school, or in the environment)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Oral hygiene 1.0 Health this week. (skill: practise one safe skill connected to Oral hygiene 1.0 Health)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Oral hygiene 1.0 Health” around your school. (skill: tell why Oral hygiene 1.0 Health matters for life in Kenya)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Oral hygiene 1.0 Health to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Oral hygiene 1.0 Health means using everyday Kenyan examples.
3. Practise this skill: describe how Oral hygiene 1.0 Health appears at home, school, or in the environment.
4. Practise this skill: practise one safe skill connected to Oral hygiene 1.0 Health.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Oral hygiene 1.0 Health from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Oral hygiene 1.0 Health: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Oral hygiene 1.0 Health?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Oral hygiene 1.0 Health means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Oral hygiene 1.0 Health means using everyday Kenyan examples.
5. Be able to: describe how Oral hygiene 1.0 Health appears at home, school, or in the environment.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
